ResponsesInList.Title: Grader Report column collapse functionality in Moodle 5.1
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Kavan, Thank you for reporting this issue and for providing details about the problem with the column collapsing in the Grader Report on Moodle 5.1. We apologize for the inconvenience caused by the text overlapping when collapsing more than three columns. Our QA team has managed to replicate the bug, and a tracker issue has been created to investigate and resolve it: MDL-87188 - Overlapping text in the collapsed columns widget in Grader report Please feel free to add any comments or vote on the issue. Thanks again for your patience and for helping improve Moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Moodle mobile app 5.1.0 beta is ready for testing
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all, The Moodle mobile app version 5.1.0 is now available on Google Play and App Store Beta channels! We value your input immensely and would love for you to help us test this new version on your own Moodle sites. Your detailed feedback is crucial for ensuring a high-quality, stable final release for the entire community. How to join the Beta programme To join the beta programme and start testing, please follow these simple steps: Install the beta app following one of these links: Android or iOS Test your experience: Log in to your Moodle site and simulate a typical student session. ResponsesInList.Title: Totally stuck with test automation
ResponsesInList.Text: The intended outcome: Building a test automation framework for front-end functional tests. Tech stack is based on: Python, Pytest, Selenium. Inspecting the HTML (DOM) of the webpage to gather elements and their respective attributes in forming Page Object Model formatting. The issue: The Test Automation Engineer was able to successfully use these tools to authenticate and land on the OKTA dashboard , then click on the <System> card. Once landed on the home page of <System>, Selenium began to give ‘NoSuchElement..’ exceptions. The Automation Engineer verified that the correct element and attributes were being used and tried in multiple ways ( CSS selector, XPATH, ID, LinkText, etc.) none of which returned a positive result. Then the tester tried other elements on the page, and same result as the previous. The troubleshooting: First instinct was to check if there was an ‘iFrame’ that we needed to switch to before accessing the element(s), that was not the case. Second strategy was to see if there was a ‘ShadowHost’ in the DOM which was causing the existence of what is called a ‘ShadowDom’. This has also been confirmed as not being the case. At least explicitly in a way that we can visually see. Third strategy was to try to use JavaScript Executor to interact with the elements, which failed, then creating a Javascript query to make sure that the javascript in the page was done loading before attempting to interact, which also failed. Needless to say, the explicit wait strategy of (wait.until.(EC….) was used throughout all of these attempts. Also, just resulting in timeouts and no actionable info.

ResponsesInList.Title: 🧡 Moodle 5.1 QA Cycle Wrap-Up
ResponsesInList.Text: We are excited to announce the completion of another successful QA cycle! Thank you all for your incredible hard work and dedication. 🌟 Cycle Highlights A huge thank you to all our testers for your commitment and effort! We completed 396 tests during this cycle, achieving an outstanding 100% pass rate 🎉 🐛 Issues Fixed During QA Thanks to the quick responses from our core developers, we were able to fix several issues during the cycle. Here’s the list of bugs that were fixed and merged: MDL-86800 - Incorrect table borders appearing across Moodle MDL-86791 - Error displayed when enabling analytics with 'mlbackend_python Use a server ' enabled on stable main MDL-86782 - Upgrade to 5.1 rc1 taking too long due blocks removal MDL-86752 - PDF Annotation line overlay in mobile view for assignment grading interface MDL-86727 - Download widget in Activity Completion report doesn't take filters into consideration MDL-86725 - Grade report search box text not visible on iOS Mobile MDL-86667 - Usability issues in the site registration form MDL-86664 - Moodle directory path shows public during installation process MDL-86596 - The profiling URL link on the breadcrumbs run by ID page is not clickable on the Boost theme MDL-86592 - CLI install error applying default setting 'analytics/predictionsprocessor' MDL-86548 - Table borders are incorrectly displayed in the glossary module 🚧 Deferred Issues A few issues identified during the QA cycle have been deferred for fixes after the release: MDL-86832 - Remove the activities block (take 2) MDL-86824 - Undefined array key exception when trying to load XMLDB files on Windows MDL-86821 - Safari iOS (iPhone 16 Pro Max): Popup menu overlaps with the table and the bar below on Gradebook setup MDL-86819 - Google Drive imports not respecting defaults MDL-86802 - OneDrive repository: Error while communicating with the repository 'File not created' MDL-86794 - Portfolio export to file success message should be similar to export to Google Drive MDL-86788 - Tiny editor autosave not working when editing existing content MDL-86784 - Adding image from public Flickr repository shows a broken image MDL-86747 - Downloading a file uploaded to Nextcloud 2 times causes an error. MDL-86733 - PHP 8.2 deprecation error in Google Drive portfolio export MDL-86726 - Incorrect confirmation "Grades were set for 0 items" when no grades are updated in Single View report MDL-86714 - 404 error being displayed on a restored SCORM activity MDL-86589 - Classic theme: No way to navigate to the dashboard if the defaulthomepage is set to 'My courses' MDL-86576 - Restoring course backup causes Essay questions with response template to save empty answers MDL-86549 - The weekly format start date alters the concept of "week Additionally, we identified a few web installation issues currently under investigation: MDL-86787 - Web installation check: composer vendor directory not found MDL-86803 - Make redirect to public folder temporary MDL-86745 - The web installation can still show public directory in some places 📘 For more information about the public directory changes, see the announcement: Upgrading to Moodle 5.1: why your site may appear broken 🔍 Additional resources: Code Restructure Directory Restructure Safe Exam Browser While testing MDLQA-20992 we uncovered a bug in the Safe Exam Browser ( SEB ) version 3.10 onwards where the audio is showing a loading loop and doesn’t play any sound. This bug has been reported to the project maintainers: https://github.com/SafeExamBrowser/seb-win-refactoring/issues/1275 🚫 Tests Marked as Non-Runners Some tests were marked as non-runners , meaning they couldn’t be executed due to external dependencies or changes in underlying functionality: MDLQA-20767 - A user can add files from Flickr MDLQA-20926 - An admin can specify the default formats for Google Drive files MDLQA-20973 - A user can add a badge earned on Moodle to their Badgr backpack MDLQA-21016 - A user can add files from Google Drive using a Workspace Google account 🏁 Final Thank You To every Moodler who contributed whether by testing, investigating, or providing fixes. Your efforts have been absolutely essential in maintaining the quality and reliability of Moodle for educators and learners worldwide. Your contributions keep our community strong and our platform excellent. Thank you once again for your dedication and teamwork and we’re already looking forward to seeing you all in the Moodle 5.2 QA cycle! 🧡 🏅 All testers will receive a QA cycle badge to celebrate your contribution, please ensure your moodle.org email address matches your Jira email.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error: Moodle boilerplate not found
ResponsesInList.Text:
Hi Joseph, when any plugin includes external libraries (we call them "third party libraries") it's good to declare their usage with a few information like name, license, version, location , external url,... To do so, you will have to create the 
```text
thirdpartylibs.
xml
```
 file in your plugin and add there all the details. You can look to any of the `thirdpartylibs.xml` files that are currently in core and you will make an idea how they look like. Then, once that file has been defined within your plugin, all the files matching the specified locations ... will be skipped by all the checks performed against the code. Hence, you will stop getting that "NoBoilerplateComment" (and other) errors. Ref.: https://moodledev.io/general/community/plugincontribution/thirdpartylibraries Ciao

ResponsesInList.Title: Why is the Behat session user different from $USER?
ResponsesInList.Text: How do you do, fellow devs. I recently ran into a few issues, while I was writing some custom Behat step definitions. I want to check that something is true for the "current user". In my own plugin code there is a function that takes the `global $USER` and checks for a record in the database related to the ID of that `$USER` . This seems like a perfectly reasonable thing to do, since `$USER` should always refer to... well... the current user. However, when I call that function from inside my Behat step definition, the `$USER` is different from the Behat session user (as returned by `behat_session_trait::get_session_user` ). To simplify, say I have an activity that users can subscribe to. I have a function in my plugin called `is_subscribed` that checks if there is a row in my subscription table with `userid = $USER->id` . Snippet of my Behat test (simplified): `And I log in as "user1"` `And I click the subscribe button...` `And I should be subscribed` That last step requires my own step definition that calls the `is_subscribed` function mentioned above. Again, very simplified: `public function i_should_be_subscribed() {` `$subscribed = is_subscribed();` `if (!$subscribed) {` `throw new ExpectationException("Not subscribed", $this->getSession());` `}` `}` The problem is that it turns out the `$USER` there is the Admin user, not "user1". Therefore the test fails. The workaround I found was to use the `set_user` method like this: `public function i_should_be_subscribed() {` `self::set_user(self::get_session_user());` `$subscribed = is_subscribed();` `self::set_user();  // reset, just in case?` `if (!$subscribed) {` `throw new ExpectationException("Not subscribed", $this->getSession());` `}` `}` The fact that `$USER` does not correspond to the Behat session user is mentioned in the documentation of `get_session_user` in passing, but I found no explanation anywhere. Maybe this is obvious, but not to me. My question is twofold: Why is this the case? Why are there two distinct "current users"? Is my approach sensible? If not, what should I do instead?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Why is the Behat session user different from $USER?
ResponsesInList.Text: This initially confused me as well (when I first started with Behat testing, many years ago), so hopefully I can help explain. There are basically 2 things going on with Behat tests. 1. A process running directly on the server - which can directly call functions and insert records in the database (and which is a single process, running continually through all your Behat tests - so you have to be careful about any static variables in your code). This is where all your step functions are run. 2. Calls which are made via the browser and which call back to the server. These are the steps that log in as a particular user and carry out steps. Each request via the browser is a separate process (just like when. a user is accessing the site normally), but session cookies retain a single user login for the duration of a particular Behat scenario (unless the scenario specifically logs out). So, steps that call functions directly on the server cannot access the $USER global for the user who is logged in via the browser, in the same way that a scheduled task running on your server wouldn't be expected to be able to access the $USER global for a user who happened to be logged into your site at the same time as the scheduled task was running. If you want to check whether a user is subscribed, then you'd need to get the step to navigate them to a page where they can see their subscription status (and then check for that text on the page). Alternatively, you could write a step that checks to see if a particular user is subscribed (e.g. And user "username" is subscribed to activity "name of activity").

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Why is the Behat session user different from $USER?
ResponsesInList.Text: The fact that these are actually two separate processes makes sense of course. I guess I just wished that whenever the Behat session user was changed, it would sync up the `global $USER` along with it in the Behat process. (I am not sure, but it seems that it does not change at all throughout the test.) But maybe that is too difficult to accomplish for some reason or would conflict with some other internal machinery. Your first suggestion is reasonable. After all, Behat tests are supposed to verify things that are visible on the page , not things that may or may not exist in the backend. So I guess the approach I took with the `is_subscribed` check inside a step function is fundamentally at odds with the testing principles here. Would you agree? The alternative would be to perform a direct DB lookup from the custom step function (without relying on `$USER` being set). Thank you!

ResponsesInList.Title: Behat command to check existence of a button?
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there such a command? I need to check a button existence by name. I tried: And I should see the button with xpath "//input[contains(@value, 'Submit and finish')]" which of course does not work. I tried: And I should see 'Submit and finish' does not work either.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat command to check existence of a button?
ResponsesInList.Text:
You are looking for 
```text
Then "Submit and finish" "button" should be visible
```
 or 
```text
Then "Submit and finish" "button" should exist
```
 The first of those reqires @ javascript , the second does not - but if you get this wrong, the error message is helpful. There are various variants of this, e.g. I click on. There is also a more elaborate forms of these, e.g. 
```text
Then "Group member" "link" should not exist in the "My links" "block"
```
 I don't know anywhere that documents the list of types of things (button, link, block, region, dialog, ...) that are aviable, other than the code: https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/lib/behat/classes/partial_named_selector.php#L60 - the comment there is not very clear, but I think the shorter list is things that can be containers, and the longer list is everything. If you scroll down, you can see how the names are translated into XPath internally. For the standard things (like button) which are provided by the core Behat libraries, you need to look elsewhere for the Xpath, if you need it: https://github.com/minkphp/Mink/blob/master/src/Selector/NamedSelector.php#L57 And, this is extensible by plugins. For example it is possible to write 
```text
And I click on "Four" "qtype_multichoice > Answer" in the "Question One" "question"
```
 and it will know how to create the Xpath for qtype_multichoice > Answer becuase of this code: https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/master/question/type/multichoice/tests/behat/behat_qtype_multichoice.php#L41 It is worth doing this for two reasons: It makes the Behat Scenarios much more readable. If you ever change the HTML for how your pluging displays things, you only need to update the behat_component_named_selector in your behat_qtype_regexpshortanswer.php, instead of updating all your scenarios.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Warning: unexpected database modification, resetting DB state
ResponsesInList.Text: Nothing should persist between separate unit tests (if it does, then there is a bug in your tests) - it should be possible to run each test separately and get exactly the same results as running all of them together. You can write helper functions (not called test_xx) which could be called from multiple tests, if you need common setup between tests (or use the setUp() function is you are wanting some same configuration for all of the tests in the file). But if you want to create a user and a course and then enrol the user in the course, then this all needs to be done within a single test.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Place of "Add a block" button
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi everyone! I want to clarify that the "Add block" button will be at the top of the block drawer, so it will always be visible when edit mode is on, regarding the height of the page or the number of blocks that are there. About the suggestion of displaying the button outside the drawer to make it "more intuitive", I can confidently say that we have tested this user flow a lot (more importantly with newcomers). We believe that we reached a balance between feature flexibility with a less steep learning curve. It's easy for us (who know and love Moodle) to move things around with the best of our intentions. However, when testings with non-moodle users, it becomes clear that we should avoid overwhelming them (and yes, adding one extra element in the UI adds tension to the decision-making process). In testings, users were more successful accomplishing their tasks when the functionalities were presented gradually to them . I hope this makes sense. Let me know your thoughts! Thanks for sharing your ideas and concerns with us! 👍

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Installation script for Behat is stuck at "-->system"
ResponsesInList.Text: If it is the 'This is not a behat test site' error, then the easiest fix is to search for that text in the code, comment out that line (if you are really sure that it _is_ your behat test site), then run: php admin/tool/behat/cli/util.php --drop (to drop all the behat tables), before running php admin/tool/behat/cli/init.php again. Remember to put the line of code that throws the error back again once you're done (I have this at least a couple of times a week, usually when I've stuffed up an install step in one of my plugins and it dies with a broken install).

Great work everyone, and thanks especially to all the new people who volunteered to help and ran tests during the weekend. As always, new testers are very welcome! Make sure you have created a tracker account then send me a message and I'll add you to the testers group. When choosing a test to run, you'll notice certain tests have labels: test_server_required means you need your own test site to run the test, as it can't be tested on the QA testing site . credentials_required means that credentials such as an OAuth 2 service client ID and secret are required for the test, which you'd need to obtain from Google or Microsoft etc. (as described in the documentation OAuth 2 services ). If you're just starting QA testing, it's good to avoid tests with these labels, as they're a bit more complicated. However if you have your own test site and / or credentials for use in testing, it's very helpful if you can choose these labelled tests, as they often get left until last!

ResponsesInList.Title: Useful tips for helping with Moodle 3.3 QA testing
ResponsesInList.Text: I just wanted to offer some advice to anyone doing Moodle 3.2 testing. When you test things, the goal is to break anything that can be broken. Using names like " Test course " is not very likely to break anything, What is much more likely to cause havoc is creating your test course (or whatever) with a name like " x < 1 && x > 0 " since bits of that can easily get confused with HTML syntax, if the code is wrong. Also, given the nature of PHP the strings " 0 " (a single digit 0) is also very likely to cause havok like MDL-50893 , MDL-53964 , MDL-16427 , MDL-44981 , MDL-20960 , MDL-35620 (Wow! I did not realise how many times this had caused a problem. Note that list is not complete.) In the past, ' (since quote) was a useful test, because of how things were stored in the database , but it is much less likely to cause issues now. Even so, ' Fergal.O'Brien@example.com ' (or similar) is a good test email address. Also, other systems are not as good as Moodle at dealing with special characters. In other systems it can be very worthwhile testing with things like ' café ' or ' 囲碁 ' but that is unlikely to be worth it in Moodle. Does anyone else have good tips for making your testing more likely to find bugs?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Useful tips for helping with Moodle QA testing
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Tim for the useful tips which I have added to the QA testing guide .

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Useful tips for helping with Moodle 3.3 QA testing
ResponsesInList.Text: Dates and times can also be difficult to handle, I had a plugin test running on travis that was working fine - except between 17h and 18h in the afternoon, then all my tests failed. The reason was simple: 17h local time = 24h Australian time, so my tests did not like the Australian midnight hour. From that moment, I regularly try as a date: 5 minutes before&after a happy new year 15 minutes before&after midnight in Sidney 29 February BTW , Gherkin Scenario Outlines are an excellent way in Behat to test several hours/dates - also the difficult ones.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Useful tips for helping with Moodle 3.3 QA testing
ResponsesInList.Text: Yes, and the days around when daylight saving starts/ends are also great times to find bugs.

ResponsesInList.Title: Suggested new Behat step for getting straight to the page you want to test
ResponsesInList.Text:
A lot of Moodle's Behat tests repeatedly test navigating around Moodle before getting to the feature they really want to test. For example: 
```text
    And I log in as "teacher"


    And I am on "Course 1" course homepage


    And I follow "Quiz 1"


    And I follow "Attempts: 1"


    And I follow "Review attempt"
```
 This is bad for several reasons: When the Moodle navigation structure changes, all our Behat tests break. This is why, at one point, the 'I am on "Course 1" course homepage' step had to be introduced to fix one breakage. The breakage that caused the '... in current page administration' to be created is another example. It makes the test take longer to run, becuase you have to load a whole lot of pages that you are not interested in testing. So, I think that we should have a step to go straight to the feature you want to test. (Of course, we should also have automated tests for how Navigation works, but we should test that once, not in every scenario.) I had a go at implementing this over at MDL-66335 / https://github.com/timhunt/moodle/compare/master...MDL-66335 . However, while the principle seems sound, I think the details need to be a bit better. In particualr, the steps like the following are not very human-readable. 
```text
    And I am on "mod_quiz" "Quiz 1" "edit"
    And I am on "mod_quiz" "Quiz 1/student/1" "attempt review"
```
 I am posting here in the hope that some people will look at what I have done, and have some good suggestions for how to make it better. Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat test in developing process
ResponsesInList.Text: Moodle HQ run all Behat tests each day, and they will now make a release unless all tests pass. Skipped tests normally relate to features that relate to feature that require a particular thing to be set up. For example the On-screen assignment grading tests can only run if you have unoconv set up on your server . If you don't have that, those tests will be skipped. So, that is probably not a worry. The failed tests are more interesting. You really need to investigate each failuer and see what went wrong. Our experience is that tests sometimes just fail randomly, so if you are running all the tests, you should use the re-run support ( https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Running_acceptance_test#Rerun_failed_scenarios ). Also, just differnet environments can cause different tests to fail. That can be worth fixing, because it basically makes Moodle more robust.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Set number of sections course in Moodle 3.3
ResponsesInList.Text: I also vote for putting this feature back into Moodle.  I have used Moodle in the past, but stopped using it for several years (because I was working on other projects).  I went back to Moodle today to begin a new site install.  I installed Moodle 3.3, and added my courses.  But I only added the course names and the descriptions -- a course catalogue.  Each course defaulted to 5 topics.  I stumbled onto this topic, and now realize that  I am going to have to uninstall Moodle 3.3 and install Moodle 3.2, because I am never going to know at the course creation how many topics / weeks are going to be in a course, and these values can be anywhere from 12 topics to courses that can have 180 days or even more.  The old way of putting in a number in the course settings for the number of topics / sections / weeks was definitely better. As for the argument about "hanging activities" that can get lost when the number of topics is reduced, there is a simple solution.  For every course, create topics+1.  The +1 topic is always the "teacher's notes" topics and is never visible to the students and can never be deleted.  If a teacher wants 5 topics, in the source code, 6 topics will actually be created -- the 5 topics for the course and the 1 topic that is the teacher's notes section.  Any time, the number of topics is reduced and there is an issue with not knowing where to put an activity, because it was in one of the topics that were deleted, those activities are placed into the "teacher's notes" section.  This is how WordPress handles side items when a person deletes a whole section from the sidebar and there are modules in that section with settings.  Those modules are not deleted.  They are just put into an administrator work area. You can also add an option to "delete empty topics" or "delete topics that are checked".   Not all teacher's create topics in order.  It is very realistic to enter in the mid-term and final project, and then fill in the other topics. Also, I think restricting the number of topics / sections is a bad idea, because you don't how exactly a teacher is going to set up a course.  But do allow the feature to indicate how many topics to display on a page.  This would be similar to a store restricting how many products are displayed on a page.  Right now it is only all topics or 1 topic. Here is scenario that is not a standard course scenario that I am currently working with.  I am creating an intensive language course.  The course is going to be 5 hours a day, 5 days a week, for 10 months.  That is a total of 1000 hours of coursework during a physical school year.  Later on I am going to have to break up this course into versions that are two hours each day; and 1 hour each day.  Right now, I am not sure if I want to set up the course with each topic being a day (4 physical hours of class time) or each topic being a physical hour of class time.  I am going to have to play around with the system to see how things can work out visually and practically. Bottom line is that the number of topics should be unlimited, but the number to display on a given page should be restricted.  If a student knows that each topic is a physical hour of class time and the course is 1000 hours long, they are not going to be "shocked", because they know that is what they are signing up for before they sign up for the course.  Or in the case of a elementary school teacher, that is just a standard school year.

New testers are always very welcome! When choosing a test to run, you'll notice certain tests have labels: test_server_required means you need your own test site to run the test, as it can't be tested on the QA testing site . credentials_required means that credentials such as an OAuth 2 service client ID and secret are required for the test, which you'd need to obtain from Google or Microsoft etc. (as described in the documentation OAuth 2 services ). If you're just starting QA testing, it's good to avoid tests with these labels, as they're a bit more complicated. However if you have your own test site and / or credentials for use in testing, it's very helpful if you can choose these labelled tests, as of course they always get left until last!

ResponsesInList.Title: Previous / Next buttons in 3.4
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm working on MDLQA-10999 It is specific to the new (reintroduced?) next and previous buttons in Moodle 3.4. Right now, the patch has been very logical about how to deal with a variety of issues. For example, even if a file resource is set to "force download " if trying to navigate to it with the next/previous button, you still get a landing page with the link, because otherwise it would break up your flow of being able to move forward and back. I think that is logical and helpful. Slightly more problematic are issues like: How should labels be considered by Left/Right navigation? How should documents with an access restriction, that are visible to students be treated? If the next activity is only available through manual completion tracking, should there be a way to mark the current activity or resource completed without returning to the course homepage? 1) I would argue that labels need to be displayed using the previous next navigation. I know the faculty where I work are used to adding little bits of information, links or text into their courses using labels. Recently in Moodle, drag and dropping of images, and media files, the default action is to create a new label, with that media embedded into the course page. In addition, since 3.3 stealth activities can be created that are linked either through URLs or more commonly through labels. Those additions have enabled faculty to use more and more labels. 2) Right now if a document has an access restriction, even if it is visible to students, next/previous navigation will skip over it and automatically go to the next piece that the user actually can view. I think that this behavior should be changed to showing the student a page with the item, and the restriction to prompt them to do whatever it is they need to do. 3) To me this is the least important of my points, but like the above two things, it can mean that the next document is actually skipping over several items with restrictions on them. I worry that students will miss things through this next/previous navigation without even realizing it. Can some more people weigh in, about what the desired behavior should be? I made a comment on MDL-59612 . I think how this is addressed will be important to how useful this new feature is in 3.4.

```text
php admin/tool/behat/cli/run.php --feature="/var/www/moodle3dev/moodle/mod/journal/tests/behat/add_entry.feature"
```
 
```text
php admin/tool/behat/cli/run.php --feature="/var/www/moodle3dev/moodle/mod/journal/tests/behat/grade_entries.feature"
```

ResponsesInList.Title: Behat config path has been changed since 3.2.2
ResponsesInList.Text: After MDL-54628 got integrated, behat directory structure has been changed a bit, so we can have more control on how behat parallel run work. behat.yml use to reside in $CFG->behat_dataroot/behat/behat.yml, From 3.2.2 it will now reside in $CFG->behat_dataroot/BEHAT_PARALLEL_SITE_NAME/behat/behat.yml Default value for BEHAT_PARALLEL_SITE_NAME is behatrun, so path is $CFG->behat_dataroot/behatrun/behat/behat.yml Similar to above for parallel runs, path will be For 1st run: $CFG->behat_dataroot/behatrun1/behat/behat.yml For 21nd run: $CFG->behat_dataroot/behatrun2/behat/behat.yml and so on. This whole change was done to manage parallel and single behat in much better way and keep information about behat within $CFG->behat_dataroot

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Help needed with Moodle 3.1 QA testing
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Alistair (et all), while it's true that still there are a number of issues which code has still not landed, this is something we were discussing/evaluating last week before deciding to proceed with the 3.1 QA round. Basically what we have done is: 1) Whenever the issues are global (not about a given plugin) (CBE issues are the main ones of this type), we have preventively failed related existing QA tests, so nobody can try them. Once the feature is complete, they will be moved back to available. 2) When the issues are confined within the limits of a plugin (say mod_feedback, or mod_lti as 2 examples of plugins having pending issues), we have allowed related QA tests to be tried. The idea is that old described behaviors should continue working in a BC way. Also, of course, if we have time... the idea is to reset them once we are feature complete, so they are re-run with the final code. 3) Apart from the two points above, that are about existing QA tests... there is a number of new tests that are being created (right now) and have not been still added to the 3.1 QA round. They describe new behaviors/features and only will be tested when we are feature complete. Basically we were discussing if was better to delay QA start or proceed with it ASAP, knowing that some test will need to be rerun (2) and will be added later (3). And looking forward to get possible problems detected earlier (and have time to fix them), we decided that starting ASAP was the best choice, with the exception of CBE (really transversal) being preventively failed to avoid problems till completed (1). Let's see how it goes, sure we learn from it, thanks for your collaboration! Ciao PS: Note I maybe slightly wrong/inaccurate with some of the points above, although I think that was, overall, the spirit of the decision. Sure that if any detail is wrong, somebody from HQ will clarify it soon.

ResponsesInList.Title: Code mess detector tuning
ResponsesInList.Text: I was recently discovering the results of the CMD tool in the travis-ci test plant. Some benefits are obvious, as some violation rules directly address missing variables, or mistyped variables, unused globals. I'm more doubting about the settings of cyclomatic and function length settings. Obviously, if you just design a very simple plugins with less then 10 files, you may not address such heavy algorithms that would need to pass the limits. Theoretical good practices would indeed pray for short functions, low number of public functions in class. that is obviously theoretic. In big plugins, promoting such good practices lead to a practical impossibility : multiply the number of function and number of small classes and you'll get an awfull to track and debug hyper-granular construct. We know one example of such implementation as Zend framework that we all know it is quickly unpenetrable. Being validating around 120 plugins of all sizes (from a small quickaccess rule to an around 100k lines integrated shop, very few of them (none in reality) would comply with the cyclomatic and complexity violations. So would'nt it be wise to soften the rules on those measurement ?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Code mess detector tuning
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Valery, I guess from your description (it's not quite clear) that you are talking about the phpmd check from moodle-plugin-ci. I've not directly used that, but there is an interesting parallel with a rule we've introduced with eslint in core with 3.2 (which is just a warning): http://eslint.org/docs/rules/complexity So would'nt it be wise to soften the rules on those measurement ? According to the phpmd docs, their warning level is 10, where as for eslint its 20 by default. Perhaps there is a case to raise the level for phpmd default in moodle-plugin-ci. In the places that eslint has found (e.g. admin/tool/lp/amd/src/tree.js ) my feeling is that is been a good indication of a code smell. When reviewing Moodle code, all too often I wish that developers would split up their functions into smaller, bite sized chunks. In general I think this is a good practice.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Travis-CI JSHint and never used functions
ResponsesInList.Text:
Without looking at the code it's hard to decide whether there is a way to write the code which will prevent the error, but one solution is that you can put in your file: 
```text
// jshint unused:false
```
 Which will disable that check for the file. Another option might be to tell jshint that you are exporting that variable (though I am not sure if this is exactly correct from your description), with: 
```text
/* exported selectcourses 
*/
```
 See jshint docs for more details Note: I've experienced various problems with jshint's detection of these situations, and we've moved to eslint for Moodle 3.2 onwards ( MDL-52127 ).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Unit test  performance
ResponsesInList.Text:
It should be possible to run all the unit tests in under an hour. I think Postgres is faster than My SQL , particularly if you follow https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Postgres_Tuning_For_Developers . The other key one is to ensure you have opcache or similar enabled when you run PHP from the command line (check by running php -i). If you are happy posting your code publicly on github, then Travis CI integration will run the unit tests for you without tying up your machine. See https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Travis_integration . Also, most of the time you don't really want to run all the unit tests. If you don't yet know it, the way to run all tests for one plugin is 
```text
vendor/bin/phpunit --testsuite mod_quiz_testsuite
```

ResponsesInList.Title: PHPUnit: mocking subplugins?
ResponsesInList.Text: Hey all, I'm fairly new to PHPUnit and I've been writing tests… that I probably should have written a while ago, but I'm currently running up against a problem. I have a polymorphic reference in one of my tables – it stores an instance id and the subplugin that instance belongs to. A lot of my code depends on those subplugins, but for kind of obvious reasons, I don't want to use the real subplugins in my test environment. This seems like a pretty clear case of "mock to the rescue" - except for this guy screwing everything up: core_plugin_manager::instance()->get_plugins_of_type The mock plugin obviously doesn't really exist, and get_plugins_of_type isn't going to load up my plugininfo subclass unless Moodle thinks that plugin is real. So my question is – how do you mock subplugins?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: PHPUnit: mocking subplugins?
ResponsesInList.Text: It depends what you are trying to test. One option: test the real code, in which case don't user mocks. Other option, only test lower-level stuff (e.g. inner workings of particular plugins) in which case, you don't need to test the part that calls plugin_manager. I notice you say you are trying to add tests to existing code. One good feature of unit testing that is not immediately obvious is that, if you write tests at the same time as you write the code, then making the code testable forces you to write it in a away where the different bits are less closely coupled. Loose coupling is often a sign of good design. Of course, that does not help you add tests to existing code.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: PHPUnit: mocking subplugins?
ResponsesInList.Text: Yeah, the problem is that the polymorphic bits of my plugin are referenced in about half of the code… that's a big hole in my code coverage. I've been thinking that I might replace any calls to get_plugins with an internal function call that can be overridden by PHPUnit and return the mocked plugin. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Parallel behat runs on seperate Selenium nodes
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks for raising this Mark, First I will start with how many parallel runs you should be running to have optimal run time. As you know you can have any number of runs initialised for behat and run them in parallel, but it's recommended to have max parallel runs = cpu_cores - 1 (1 less then the number of cpu cores), so each run gets a cpu. To answer you first question, there are few factors which can reduce the random fails. FYI : It's hard to get zero random fails all the time as it depends lot on your system resources. Ensure max parallel runs is less then number of cpu cores - 1. (Personally 3 parallel runs are optimal) Use xvfb or xvnc or docker to avoid browser display on your screen. This might lead to focus fails if you are working on the system. Finally use --rerun to eliminate any random fails each run. (Will share the code which we use later.) To run multiple Selenium servers on different displays and behat parallel run to use them, follow the following: Set following in your config.php (before including setup.php). For more information about other params refer https://docs.moodle.org/dev/Acceptance_testing#Advanced_usage $CFG->behat_parallel_run = array ( array ('wd_host' => ' http://127.0.0.1:4444/wd/hub' ), array ('wd_host' => ' http://127.0.0.1:4445/wd/hub' ), array ('wd_host' => ' http://127.0.0.1:4446/wd/hub' ) ); Start selenium using xvfb (you can use docker or xvnc) xvfb-run -a java -jar PATH_TOSELENIUM/selenium-server.jar -port 4444 xvfb-run -a java -jar PATH_TOSELENIUM/selenium-server.jar -port 4445 xvfb-run -a java -jar PATH_TOSELENIUM/selenium-server.jar -port 4446 initialise behat with 3 parallel runs and when you run using admin/tool/behat/cli/run.php it will use different selenium ports. Even with the above approach, I have observed few random fails at times. Saying so dividing the runs between docker instances works 99% of the time without any problem. You can use "php admin/tool/behat/cli/run.php --fromrun=2 --torun=2" to run specific run on a docker instance and 99% of the times the run will pass without any problem. Finally the script which I use is https://gist.github.com/rajeshtaneja/475d923fd482311c1544 , where I get exit codes and check rerun files to run behat one after other in sequence to eliminate random fails.

ResponsesInList.Title: Behat smashes the whole database every time I run it, so I cannot test my Atto plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi all I'm still fighting with Behat :P I want to test my Atto plugin. So, I configure the editor to put it on the toolbar. This configuration is stored on behat_config_plugins (or whatever prefix) table , in the value column , for plugin='editor_atto' and name='toolbar' rows. But, when I run Behat, even for my @atto_mybutton plugin only, before executing the tests, all table data is deleted and after re-inserted as default was, so my plugin won't be visible, making the test fail. And, also, needing much time for running the test (sometimes more than a minute for a single simple test). I don't know if this is the correct behaviour; I haven't seen nothing about this in the docs . But, the thing is that, apart from needing excessive time for executing the tests, this doesn't allow to tests my own plugins. Any type of help will be gratefully appreciated. Best regards, Julen

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat smashes the whole database every time I run it, so I cannot test my Atto plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: The whole point of behat tests is that they start with a clean install then run the steps that you have provided - this makes the tests consistent and repeatable. If some extra configuration is needed, then you need to include that in your behat test. You will probably find something like this helpful: And I log in as "admin" And I set the following administration settings values: | name_of_setting | value_of_setting | OR And the following config values are set as admin: | name_of_setting | value_of_setting | (The first logs in as admin, then searches for the setting and then sets it in the UI, the second pushes the value directly into the database , without going via the UI)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat smashes the whole database every time I run it, so I cannot test my Atto plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Oh, now I see it, I have to add in the test the process I would follow for the configuration. The whole database install was misleading me, but know I see it clear. Lot of thanks, Davo. Julen

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat smashes the whole database every time I run it, so I cannot test my Atto plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: By the way, is there any option to make Behat not reinstall the whoooole database from the scratch (without touching the core...)? It supposes a considerable overhead, and many times is not interesting to test with a clean installation. Best regards, Julen

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat smashes the whole database every time I run it, so I cannot test my Atto plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: No. If nothing has changed, then the previous snapshot of the database is used. If something has changed (i.e. one of the version.php files has been updated), then a clean install is needed and a new snapshot is created. You *always* want to test with a clean installation, otherwise you may end up with inconsistent tests. Anyway, with suitable hardware + postgres DB, the complete installation should only take about 30 seconds or so (maybe 60 seconds - a bit more if doing lots of tests in parallel).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat smashes the whole database every time I run it, so I cannot test my Atto plugin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Julen, The database & dataroot state must be the same, if you feel like many times it is not interesting to test with a clean installation is because you have dependencies between scenarios, you can share parts of a feature using the Background section. To complement Davo's reply; if by "reinstall" you mean the database & dataroot reset between scenarios (it should be around 2 secs though) you can always create a spaghetti scenario testing all your code in 1 single scenario. This is not ideal, but you "can" do it.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Testing with Behat, I run into a moodle exception
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Mariana, As behat is supposed to catch any exception/debugging message thrown on the page, it checks after each step. (behat_hooks::i_look_for_exception()), so there is no way you can bypass this. As this is a local plugin, rather then throwing exception, in debug mode you can return text saying this page is not accessible by user.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Testing with Behat, I run into a moodle exception
ResponsesInList.Text: Is there a way for me to catch or incorporate this exception into a step?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Testing with Behat, I run into a moodle exception
ResponsesInList.Text: With current implementation, code is executed from moodle-behat-extension after every step, to catch any debugging or exception on page. So it's beyond the scope of step to catch exception. Please feel free to open an issue on tracker, so step can allow exceptions to be caught. But with current way, you need to either fix your code to not throw exception or check valid state only.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Error writing to database
ResponsesInList.Text:
This error means that it tried to insert more data than your MySQL configuration allows. If you find your my.cnf file and open it with a text editor, it should hold the following parameter: 
```text
max_allowed_packet
```
 Change the value there to 
```text
max_allowed_packet = 32M
```
 And restart MySQL, that should make sure that the insert can be done without issues.

ResponsesInList.Title: How to run individual tests using behat
ResponsesInList.Text: Can someone guide me if we can run Individual tests using Behat and moodle. I am unable to run individual tests. Any help regarding this is highly appreciated.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to run individual tests using behat
ResponsesInList.Text: You can choose which tests to run, by using the 'tags' command. e.g. vendor/bin/behat --config /path/to/behat.yml --tags '@mod_forum,@mod_assign' (this assumes that the relevant tests exist and have been tagged appropriately - I haven't checked) If you want to run just a single test, then the easiest thing to do is to edit the x.feature file and put @runonlythis (or whatever you want to call the tag) just before the 'Scenario:' line, then use the line: vendor/bin/behat --config /path/to/behat.yml --tags @runonlythis

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to run individual tests using behat
ResponsesInList.Text: Actually, to run a single feature file, do vendor/bin/behat --config /path/to/behat.yml /path/to/test/behat/file.feature And, if you don't know about it, you almost certainly want to add something like $CFG-> behat_faildump_path = '/tmp/behat_failures'; to your config.php file. That way, every time a test fails, you will get a screen-grab in that folder of the moment when it went wrong.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: How to run individual tests using behat
ResponsesInList.Text:
Note than in order run a single feature file, it appears you need to use the fully qualified path to the file like so: 
```text
vendor/bin/behat --config /path/to/behat.yml $(pwd)/path/to/test/behat/file.feature
```
 You can also run specific scenarios within the file by supplying a starting and (optional) ending line number: 
```text
vendor/bin/behat --config /path/to/behat.yml $(pwd)/path/to/test/behat/file.feature:123-321
```

Is there a workaround for this already implemented in Behat, or would I have to write it myself? Thanks.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: How do I select from two buttons with the same value?
ResponsesInList.Text:
You can click a css element in a css element. For example: 
```text
I click on "a" "css_element" in the "div.viewlink" "css_element"
```
 Or, if the item you want to click is already unique by some css selector, you can simply use something like: 
```text
I click on "div.viewlink a" "css_element"
```
 It really depends on the DOM where you want to click. hth

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: How do I select from two buttons with the same value?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks! Worked like a charm.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: How do I select from two buttons with the same value?
ResponsesInList.Text: While you can do this (and there is also xpath_element for when you need really tricky selectors), it is not necessarily the right thing to do. The reason to think more deeply is because of accessibility . It is not just Behat that needs to work out which button to click from only the text label. Users who require a screen-reader also have to work something like that. Therefore, that fact that you find it difficult to write a Behat script to use the UI should also make you worry about how the UI is for disabled users. Perhaps the real fix here is to change one or both or the button labels. Perhaps it should be "Create sub-folder of 'Folder 1'" and "Create folder"?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat cli doesn't execute features from sub-folders in 2.9?
ResponsesInList.Text: What do you mean ' root features folder'? The place you are supposed to put .feature files is path/to/plugin /tests/behat/something.feature and that can work even with quite a lot of .feature files: https://github.com/moodle/moodle/tree/master/mod/quiz/tests/behat What file layout are you trying to use?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat cli doesn't execute features from sub-folders in 2.9?
ResponsesInList.Text: The place we are supposed to put .feature files is path/to/plugin /tests/behat and while this can work with many feature files, in some cases it may be more manageable to add a logical division within that place, e.g. path/to/plugin /tests/behat/cat1 path/to/plugin /tests/behat/cat2 path/to/plugin /tests/behat/cat1/cat1.1 etc. This is possible in 2.8 b/c there the yml lists the feature places (folders) rather than particular feature files. In 2.9 it lists particular files but it doesn't take files from sub-folders.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat cli doesn't execute features from sub-folders in 2.9?

If you want a simple work-around, just make a naming patter like I did for the quiz tests, with several related .feature files with names that start the same, like attempt_{details}.feature or editing_{details}.feature. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat cli doesn't execute features from sub-folders in 2.9?
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Itamar and Tim for raising this. This is related to MDL-39752 , as we are now specifying each feature file as part of this fix, so they can be divided for parallel runs. Moodle by default doesn't support feature files to be placed under sub-directory. If you want to include more feature files, you should use $CFG->behat_additionalfeatures. It was working before, because we used to just set file paths and behat was recursively searching for feature files within those paths.

ResponsesInList.Title: Behat: Writing Single Given-When-Then in Gherkin
ResponsesInList.Text: You may be aware of a point of contention about our recommendation for only a single Given/When/Then in behat feature files following this guidance: http://docs.behat.org/en/latest/guides/1.gherkin.html I have started a policy issue about this issue: MDL-48186 Feel free to comment here or in the issue!

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: Writing Single Given-When-Then in Gherkin
ResponsesInList.Text: I'd be really interested to hear from anyone who is using this kind of test specification in other environments - or knows examples from other open source projects with the size and complexity we have?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: Writing Single Given-When-Then in Gherkin
ResponsesInList.Text: I have been thinking about this recently, and while in general I can see that it is good to test one thing per scenario (so then, if something fails, you know exactly what failed, and can re-run just that specific thing when you think you have fixed it) I don't believe it is acutally possible in practice. The example I came across recently where I thought it was not reasonable to do just one thing per scenario was testing questoin preview: https://github.com/moodle/moodle/blob/234c5337f7b562465568458422a5de5a7146e8b7/question/tests/behat/preview_question.feature When previewing a question some things can naturally only be done after other things. If you believe it is possible to break up that feature file into separate scenarios that only test one thing each, then please show me how by rewriting that file. Note that that feature file would be much more readable if each block for lines from line 40 onwards would be easier to read if it started with another When, and switched back to Then at the appropriate point.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: Writing Single Given-When-Then in Gherkin
ResponsesInList.Text:
Just to say that Rajesh replied in the tracker issue , taking up my challenge. His re-working of my script was pretty good, and having seen it I realised that I could then do even better. So, as part of MDL-48373 I found time to covert all the question Behat tests to the approved style. The real point of this post is to report on what I found. What I was really doing was creating proper generators for questions, so you can say And the following "questions" exist: in the set-up for your scenario. This should make things faster than the old way of creating things through the Moodle UI. On the other hand, splitting the existing long rambling tests into separate ones makes things slower, becuase we reset and repeat the initialisation more often. Also, while working on these scripts I notices a few things were missed out in the testing, and added them. So, overall, the run-time (for --tags core_question) has gone from 
```text
9 scenarios (9 passed)


288 steps (288 passed)


4m54.203s
```
 to 
```text
28 scenarios (28 passed)


462 steps (462 passed)


7m5.508s
```
 So, from 5 mins to 7 mins. . On the other hand, when something failes, you can just re-run that one specific test which is much shorter . Overall, I think the new tests are better. So, I am starting to believe that 'Test one things per scenario' is not only desirable, but also possible. However, I still think that if you are testing more than one things per scenario, you should be allowed to use more than one When and Then because it is much easier to read.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: Writing Single Given-When-Then in Gherkin
ResponsesInList.Text:
However, I still think that if you are testing more than one things per
scenario, you should be allowed to use more than one When and Then
because it is much easier to read. Indeed. But even testing one thing may require more than one Then/When. For instance, if I need to test a feature of Group submission that allows group members to work on the same entry, I need multiple logins in the same scenario. Multiple logins invite multiple "Then" (I don't use "When" at all; one opening Given and then Thens and Ands). To make the scenario more readable I also add a substantial amount of inline comments. I even use code folding for which I define special "comments" such as #section: to open and #:section to close.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: Writing Single Given-When-Then in Gherkin
ResponsesInList.Text: What you say shows that you have not yet got the right mind-set. What you describe is a number of different scenarios: One student can submit a first version of a group assignment. Another student can add to a group assignment started by another student in their group. One student in the group can complete their group's assignment. Etc. (To make this feasible, you need set-up steps, so you can can quickly set up the starting situation for the second and later scenarios.)

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: Writing Single Given-When-Then in Gherkin
ResponsesInList.Text: Whether what I describe is one scenario or a composite of several scenarios is merely terminological and is really not the issue. Many scenarios can be steps in bigger scenarios and at least some of our current core steps are such. You seem to suggest that for many Gherkin scenarios we need to write their php counterpart only to make complex scenarios look simple. That shouldn't be our preferred approach because it may be counter productive. And don't get me wrong. I'm already adding many "set up" steps to make the tests more efficient. But in general it is not the way. Gherkin may at some point allow re-use of scenarios within scenarios and at any rate it shouldn't be too difficult to add a pseudo step that would do that. The point remains that for some scenarios it may not be worth it to reproduce Gherkin in php only to maintain the Single Given-When-Then convention.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: Writing Single Given-When-Then in Gherkin
ResponsesInList.Text: To be sure, I don't really have a problem with this styling convention. I can work around it and continue to comply with Moodle coding guidelines just like I worked around the weird requirement, in my opinion, to put a full stop at the end of an inline comment even when the inline comment is meant as a label rather than a descriptive statement. ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: Writing Single Given-When-Then in Gherkin
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Itamar, As you know b ehat doesn't technically distinguish between these three kind of steps, so you can use what best suite your need. In Moodle core, it's good that we are sticking to single GIVEN-WHEN-THEN, as this try to enforce that single scenario should not be testing more then what is described in scenario outline. Also, force developer to write multiple scenarios covering specific functionality and not miss coverage. If you think you need multiple WHEN then probably you need to re-visit your scenario and see if you are trying to test more then what you were expecting in scenario. We know that we have a drawback of maintaining more code and increase run time, but advantage is the coverage report. If you are testing enrol_user then what all scenarios are covered is clearly visible from scenario list and you don't have to read behat feature file to understand it. FYI : Robert C. Martin has written a great post about BDD's Given-When-Then concept where he thinks of them as a finite state machine. Also, behat 3 doesn't support step chaining and sub- context , making it hard to have a pseudo-step. https://github.com/Behat/Behat/issues/546 https://github.com/Behat/Behat/issues/558#issuecomment-65213657

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: Writing Single Given-When-Then in Gherkin
ResponsesInList.Text: Thanks Rajesh. I think that Moodle core perspective, as you posit it here, actually misses something in the point of BDD reflecting the requirements analysis process/language. Developers see discrete functions/features as singular scenarios. Subject matter experts see wholes of complext situations. An obvious shortcoming of the the various blog posts is that they give simple examples that are easy to fit into the over-simplification of the Single Given-When-Then model. Some of the replies to the posts point that out. So, the proposed convention may serve a purpose in the context of Moodle core development, but this doesn't mean that it would be as effective in other contexts of Moodle development. But at the end of the day, all this can be merely academic. If you plan to make the code checker generate errors/warnings about this convention, please add an option to ignore this convention so that it doesn't interfere with plugins' compliance with Moodle coding guidelines.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: Writing Single Given-When-Then in Gherkin
ResponsesInList.Text: I've been writing a number of Behat tests recently for projects I've been working on. I've found very few situations in which a single given..when..then would make sense. For example, I've done a lot around modifications to the facetoface module within Totara - that often involves, for example, a teacher logging in and setting up a session with dates, then a student logging in and signing up to a session, then the teacher logging in and checking that the student appears correctly, then cancelling the student sign up, then the student logging in to check they have been cancelled. Ideally that would be 5 tests: Test the teacher can log in and set up a face to face session Test the student can log in and sign up to a session Test the teacher can see students who have signed up for a session Test the teacher can cancel students who have signed themselves up to a session Test the student can see that they've been removed from a session However, to split those into 5 tests, each of those tests would have to include all the steps from the previous tests in the 'given' section (aside from a couple of lines at the end that check the correct output is shown on the screen). To my mind that makes the file harder to read (as there are large amounts of repeated statements to wade through) and will certainly make the already slow Behat tests run even more slowly (which is an important practical consideration). Whilst I sympathise with the ideal (maybe with expanded use of generators, or in areas with less complex workflows it might be achievable), I'd much prefer the readability of multiple When ... Then ... sections (especially if there are comments before each section to introduce what is being tested in that part).

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: Writing Single Given-When-Then in Gherkin
ResponsesInList.Text:
Davo, I believe the 'correct' solution to that scenario is to extend the generators, so you for scenario 2. you can start efficiently by saying: 
```text
Given the following 'activity' exists
  | facetoface | ... |
And the following 'face-to-face' sessions exist
  ...
```
 However, that is a bit more work. The pay-back would be when your behat test is failing at point 5. With one long scenario, you have a long wait every time you run the test, so see if you have now fixed it. With separate scenarios, you can just run step 5.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Assumptions about unit tests
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Tim, My view: 1/2. I'd like to think that Moodle unit tests should work with any combination of plugins installed. But I don't think its straight forward working out who's responsibility it is to deal with this. Sometimes I think the plugin will need to take the responsibility to maintain the normal state during phpunit tests. There is a lot of config state in Moodle, we know how many setting there are and if you had to verify state of every single one of them before beginning your test, you'd make the test unreadable. Can't think of a good example off the top of my head, but lets say your plugin enabled an imaginary $CFG->disableallpermissionchecks I think it'd be unreasonable for every single test involving permissions to verify that. (Especially because there might be 10 similar flags which could affect the result). 3. More importantly, we'd very unlikely spot it. 4. Or maybe if its really problematic and doesn't affect your plugin, you could wrap the state altering changes in a PHPUNIT_TEST or choose a different approach where it only happens when the plugin is enabled? Another example would be a behat test - you might have a plugin which has an event listener which unenrols a student from a course when they get something wrong - would it be reasonable for the behat tests be able to deal with any situation caused by things like that?

ResponsesInList.Text: Andrea, the testing framework is a Java project. We chose Java over PHP because we wanted to try Selenium 2 WebDriver and PHP is not officially supported by SeleniumHQ anymore, whereas Java is. The unofficial PHP language bindings had some limitations and the documentation wasn't great. It's still early days but so far I have been working on object repositories from the default, vanilla Moodle install to be used in conjunction with the integration process. Hopefully the project will be available on GitHub today if all goes to plan. I've left Moodle acceptance tests in there as examples. I have tried to refactor as much as possible to simplify things. I'm trying to make the page objects handle Moodle with Javascript turn on and off and also handle other unpredictable events. The strategy for locators is to try the following: 1) locate by unique, static id. If not possible e.g. id='submit' can't really be used because it is present on many submit buttons: 2) locate by unique, static css selector (selectors that can be displayed on the web page such as the value selector must be passed from properties file). If not possible e.g. more than one object sharing CSS Selectors on the same page: 3) locate by onscreen text using xpath e.g. //a[contains(.,'some text')] to locate a link with 'some text' passed from properties files, or from tests using parameters (and test data properties) if the link was created by the test itself. Recently I refactored some of my more complicated methods into utility methods in a bid to reduce the number of lines of code in the page objects. ResponsesInList.Text: Hello, We recently upgraded to PHP 5.5 on our Debian server so as to use OPcache. Unfortanetly, we haven't seen much improvement in performance.  Here is a screenshot of the OPcache Overview page: http://screencast.com/t/V2MvjlY9F Notice that Memory Usage is at 100%. I've searched the web but can't figure out this is good or bad. Can anyone shed some light on this? Also, does this screenshot reveal any other problems? I should also mention that we are using a virtual server with 4MB RAM and we are running 2 Moodle sites (version 2.4 and 2.5). Any feedback would be appreciated. Thanks, Fernando

ResponsesInList.Text: Not quite my area of expertise Fernando, but you may find this forum is also helpful: https://moodle.org/mod/forum/view.php?id=596 -Derek

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: OPcache: Memory Usage = 100% (is this good or bad?)
ResponsesInList.Text: Hello Fernando, looking at the screenshot provided I think you could probably increase the memory used by OPCache so you could cache more files, currently you have 'opcache.max_accelerated_files=4000' however most probably you reached almost 100% of cache consumption with less than 4000 files. You can check the number of currently cached file using the "File usage" button on the OPCache gui script, then you could try increasing OPCache memory of about 64MB and verify if your hit rate increases.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: OPcache: Memory Usage = 100% (is this good or bad?)
ResponsesInList.Text: What is that "OPCache gui script" that you referred to? Where do I find this gui script in Moodle 2.7.2? Thank you.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: OPcache: Memory Usage = 100% (is this good or bad?)
ResponsesInList.Text: I'm just learning about this myself but... I think you're fine. You ideally want to be using just under 100%. Any less and you're wasting memory that could by used by other things (assuming you've got it on the same machine as something else), any more and it'll start bumping things out of the cache. It looks like you've just hit the bumping things out of the cache level, but memcached is smart enough to ditch the least useful things. For example I noticed that if you update your language strings then the cache will immediately get about 1000 new entries for each of the language files. But they're not used in the normal flow of use so you don't care of those 1000 get bumped out of the cache in favor of things that are hit more often. Keep an eye on the hit rate. At first it'll be low since the first time any file gets fetched that counts as a miss, so it's entirely expected for there to be a few thousand misses as the cache warms up. But I'd expect it to move up to 99% if things are working okay and those initial misses get dwarfed by the later repeated hits.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: how do teachers enrol cohorts?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Having a look at the code I see that you can only enrol cohorts defined in a context where your user has moodle/cohort:view capability. Techers have this capability assigned by default at course level (course context). But you can only define cohorts at the system or category level. So that means that regular course teachers cannot enrol cohorts Whether this is a bug or a design feature is open to debate . I suspect the reason it works the way it does is because cohort enrolment can be thought of as category (or site-wide) "management". Then it would makes sense to assign that capability at the category or site level to those people in charge of that "management". But feel free to open a bug if you think the current behaviour is not that useful for most people Saludos.
Iñaki.

ResponsesInList.Title: File Size Limits in Repository
ResponsesInList.Text: I have a large file (25.3 MB) I would like to load into Moodle 2.0 2RC1 using the Repository and the local ( server ) file system.  It's easy to get it into the local file system, but when I try to make it available in a folder as a resource in moodle it gives me an error message saying the file is bigger than the maximum size. I can't find anywhere in the moodle configuration information about what the size limit is or how to change it.  If I was uploading a file, I would guess that the PHP upload size limits would be an issue (set to 10 MB on my server), but that doesn't seem like it ought to apply for a file already on the server.  Is there an articifical limit being enforced somewhere by moodle?  If so, can it be changed somehow?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: File Size Limits in Repository
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Steve, Just wondering whether the maximum upload size for the course (in the course settings) is preventing you from including the file as a resource in your course?

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: File Size Limits in Repository
ResponsesInList.Text: It may be that the PHP upload limit is the problem, but if so that seems like a bad design decision.  I'll test it a little and see if lowering the limit further restricts the files I can add.  The reason I think limiting Repository transfers from local files in this way is a bad design decision is that instructors sometimes need to add data to the course which is larger than the PHP upload limit.  The maximum upload size you can set from inside moodle is limited by the maximum PHP upload size.  Some sites won't have an easy ability to change this. A work-around for this limitation in pre-moodle 2.0 verions was to transfer the file directly to the moodledata directory on the server and make it accessible from there.  With the new file system, it seems like the equivalent action would be to put the file in a directory on the server and use the Repository to get it into moodle.  If such a transfer is limited by the PHP file upload limit, it is hard to see how users could easily get a file larger than this limit into moodle.

ResponsesInList.Title: Behat: How to get a custom generator?
ResponsesInList.Text:
Given the Behat rule file "local/more_rules/tests/behat/behat_local_core_rules.php" and the generator file "local/more_rules/tests/generator/lib.php". The rules class is build with 
```text
class behat_local_more_rules extends behat_base {}
```
 The generator class is build with 
```text
class local_more_rules_generator extends testing_data_generator {}
```
 To be able to call the generator methods I need the reference to the generator class. In "lib/tests/behat/behat_data_generators.php" I found the line that gets the datagenerator 
```text
$this->datagenerator = testing_util::get_data_generator();
```
 When I call the same line in my rules script I get an error. My solution for now is to hard code the connection to the generator with 
```text
require_once(__DIR__.'/../generator/lib.php');


$this->generator = new local_more_rules_generator();
```
 This code works but I hope there might be a more general solution.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat: How to get a custom generator?
ResponsesInList.Text:
```text
$this->datagenerator = testing_util::get_data_generator()->get_plugin_generator('local_more_rules');
```
 hth

ResponsesInList.Title: Behat and custom roles
ResponsesInList.Text: We are starting to write our own Behat tests and it has been going pretty well. However, one of the problems we are coming up against is the need to use custom roles while doing tests for our plugins. We have customized Instructor, Teaching Assistant, and several "guests" roles that we want to be automatically tested. What is the best approach for loading custom roles in a Behat environment? We are running Moodle 2.5.4.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat and custom roles
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rex, Good to hear that What you can do with the current step definitions is to follow the required step to create a new role, this would be useful if you would just need to test a couple of features related with your custom role, but I guess that you, like many other organizations using custom roles, would base most of your scenarios on these roles so you need a quicker way to set them up; if you are interested in always having the same custom roles in each scenario you can create a new step Given I add rex custom roles or even more generic Given I add rex data set in local/rexrules/tests/behat/behat_local_rexrules.php and use PHP code to generate all you need, using testing data generators or direct Moodle APIs calls, then each feature requiring these datasets can include it. Note that this approach (to use PHP code to set data) goes against the black-box principle of acceptance testing so, at a practical level, you should restrict the use of this steps to the Given section (settingthe scenario contexts). An addition, what I would be happy to include in core would be a data generator for create roles, as I guess more organizations would be interested in using it. ( https://tracker.moodle.org/browse/MDL-44108 ) Regards, David

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat and custom roles
ResponsesInList.Text: David, I took a look at the tracker ticket you created and this wouldn't exactly solve our problem. We already are currently just renaming the existing roles to match the role shortnames our custom code is looking for. However, the next step we want to do automated testing is the certain capabilities that our custom roles have set. I know that Moodle 2.6 introduced role export/import and would like to see some Moodle core support to specify the importing of these role definitions, similar to the way there are very easy backup/restore steps already defined that do all the heavy lifting of uploading a backup and selecting the appropriate settings.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat and custom roles
ResponsesInList.Text: Hi Rex, If you want to override capabilities we also have a data generator for it ( http://docs.moodle.org/dev/Acceptance_testing#Available_elements - Permission overrides) you can automate it as I commented above using a rex custom step, or also you could add a step definition with the @BeforeScenario annotation so it will be auto executed, but I am thinking that you will need to ensure that it is executed after behat_hooks::before_scenario which resets the database and the dataroot directory status.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat and custom roles
ResponsesInList.Text: David, I try to understand your feedback - can you please explain why you call the proposed feature "rexrules"? I guess the name has a meaning but I don't understand it may be important.

ResponsesInList.Title: Re: Behat and custom roles
ResponsesInList.Text: Afaict the name doesn't have a particular meaning. The idea is that you can create tests for core components with steps that are not provided by core, by adding a local plugin (e.g. local_mysteps, local_davidrules etc.) defining the steps there and then writing the tests with those additional steps.

ResponsesInList.Title: Commenting out multiple lines in acceptance test feature
ResponsesInList.Text:
When writing a long scenario with repeating steps in an acceptance test feature I sometimes want to try only a certain part of the scenario, as running the whole scenario may be time consuming (scenario outlines are not a viable option as they repeat too much). Using # to comment out lines may be tedious. Gherkin doesn't seem to support block comments. I found at http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7113594/how-to-do-block-comments-in-gherkin , item 7, a suggestion to use PyStrings type comments, which seems to work quite nicely. So for example, all the steps in the illustration below will be ignored when running the feature. 
```text
"""


        When I go to manage dataform "views"


        And I follow "id_editview1"


        And I expand all fieldsets       


        And I fill textarea "Entry template" with "
Checkbox 01
\n
EAC:edit
\n
EAC:delete
"


        And I press "Save changes"


        And I follow "Browse"


        And I follow "id_editentry1"


        And I set the field "CB 01" to "checked"


        And I press "Save"


        Then I should see "CB 01"


        ...


"""
```
 In this particular scenario I have about 11 50-steps sections and as I'm adding each section I'm commenting out all others (except for the opening section that is needed for all the others) and trying only that part before adding the next sections.
